t.1.50.2: The eldest son of Gautama, whose radiance was made to shine by his austerities, was filled with the greatest wonder at the mere sight of Rāma.
t.1.50.1: Having heard those words of the wise Viśvāmitra, the greatly radiant Śatānanda, a man of great austerity, felt his hair stand on end with joy.
t.1.50.3: Seeing the two princes seated and comfortably settled, Śatānanda then spoke to Viśvāmitra, the foremost of sages.
t.1.50.4: O tiger among sages, was my illustrious mother, who had undertaken long austerities, shown by you to the prince?
t.1.50.5: O greatly splendid one, did my illustrious mother offer worship with the fruits of the forest to Rāma, who is worthy of the worship of all embodied beings?
t.1.50.6: O greatly radiant one, has the ancient affair of my mother, the wrong done to her by the god, been told to Rāma just as it happened?
t.1.50.7: Kauśika, may good fortune be yours! O best of sages, has my mother been reunited with my father through beholding Rāma here?
t.1.50.8: O son of Kuśika, was Rāma honored by my venerable father? Has the greatly radiant one come here after receiving worship from that great-souled one?
t.1.50.10: Having heard those words of his, the great sage Viśvāmitra, skilled in speech, replied to Śatānanda, who was himself well versed in speech.
t.1.50.9: O son of Kuśika, was my revered elder respectfully saluted by Rāma, who came here devout and with a tranquil mind?
t.1.50.12: Having heard those words of the wise Viśvāmitra, the greatly radiant Śatānanda spoke these words to Rāma.
t.1.50.11: Nothing has been neglected, O best of sages; what had to be done has been done by me. The wife has been reunited with the sage, just as Reṇukā was with Bhārgava.
t.1.50.13: Welcome to you, O best of men! By good fortune you have arrived, O Rāghava, placing at your head Viśvāmitra, the unconquered great sage.
t.1.50.14: Viśvāmitra, whose deeds are beyond imagining, a brahmarṣi through his austerity, of boundless radiance and great power: you know him to be the supreme refuge.
t.1.50.15: O Rāma, there is no one else on earth more fortunate than you, for your protector is the son of Kuśika, by whom great austerity has been performed.
t.1.50.16: Listen, and I shall relate the strength of the great-souled Kauśika and all that happened just as it occurred; hear it from me as I tell it.
t.1.50.17: This one was for a long time a king of righteous soul, a subduer of enemies, knowing dharma and accomplished in learning, and devoted to the welfare of his subjects.
t.1.50.18: There was a king named Kuśa, a son of Prajāpati. Kuśa's son was the mighty and most righteous Kuśanābha.
t.1.50.19: Kuśanābha's son was renowned by the name of Gādhi. Gādhi's son is the great sage Viśvāmitra, of great splendour.
t.1.50.20: The greatly lustrous Viśvāmitra protected the earth; for many thousands of years the king ruled the kingdom.
t.1.50.21: Once, that greatly splendid one, having marshalled his army and surrounded by an akṣauhiṇī, roamed about the earth.
t.1.50.22: Wandering through cities and kingdoms, rivers and mountains as well, the king came in due course to the hermitages.
t.1.50.23: He saw the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha, with trees bearing many kinds of flowers and fruits, crowded with herds of various animals, and frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.
t.1.50.24: It was adorned by Devas, Dānavas, Gandharvas and Kiṃnaras, crowded with tranquil deer, and frequented by flocks of birds.
t.1.50.25: He came to the hermitage crowded with hosts of brahmarṣis and frequented by hosts of devarṣis, great-souled beings who had attained perfection through the practice of austerities and who shone like fire.
t.1.50.26: It was ever thronged with glorious great-souled sages equal to Brahmā, some living on water alone, some on air, and others on withered leaves.
t.1.50.27: It was thronged with ṛṣis and Vālakhilyas who lived on fruits and roots, who were self-restrained, who had conquered anger and subdued their senses, and who were wholly devoted to japa and homa.
t.1.50.28: The mighty Viśvāmitra, best of victors, beheld the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha, which was like another world of Brahmā.
